staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced the crash against this staged vulnerable checkout. Its line map matches the saved ASan frames at `internal_huf.c:1186`, `internal_huf.c:1284`, `internal_huf.c:1799`, and `internal_piz.c:624`, and the local `patch.diff` adds the missing `currByte >= topByte` guard in the `LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN` branch.

classification.classification_note: Both saved crash traces report `heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 1` in `fasthuf_read_bits()`. The exact allocated chunk-buffer size differs between the two saved builds, but the faulting statement and call chain are the same.

bug_description.original: A heap-buffer-overflow (out-of-bounds read) occurs in src/lib/OpenEXRCore/internal_huf.c: the fasthuf_read_bits routine (invoked from fasthuf_initialize during Huffman table parsing and used by internal_huf_decompress / internal_exr_undo_piz) can read past the end of the input buffer when processing malformed or truncated Huffman table data. This can cause crashes or potential information disclosure during decompression.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable worktree `_work/src`
bug_description.normalized: The reproduced witness is a PIZ-compressed OpenEXR file processed by `exrcheck -s -c`. After the file is accepted onto the PIZ decompression path, `internal_exr_undo_piz()` extracts the Huffman-coded sub-buffer and `internal_huf_decompress()` parses its header, derives the table start pointer, and enters `fasthuf_initialize()` to read per-symbol code lengths. Vulnerable `fasthuf_initialize()` checks `currByte >= topByte` before each initial 6-bit `codeLen` read, but if that 6-bit value is `LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN` it immediately calls `fasthuf_read_bits(8, ...)` for the run length without repeating the end-of-buffer guard. On the crashing path the long-zero-run marker is accepted at the end of the admitted table bytes, so the second read refills from `currByte == topByte` and `fasthuf_read_bits()` dereferences one byte past the heap-backed packed chunk buffer. The fix adds the missing `currByte >= topByte` check in the `LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN` branch and returns `EXR_ERR_CORRUPT_CHUNK` for truncated table data.

source.description: First project-side materialization of vulnerability-relevant attacker data on the reproduced path. The PIZ decoder reads the next 32-bit field from the packed chunk as the byte length of the Huffman-coded payload that will be handed to `internal_huf_decompress()`.
source.value_from: The reproduced command is `/gt/_work/build/bin/exrcheck -s -c /gt/poc`. In `exrCheck()` the CLI reads the 199-byte PoC into `vector<char> data` and calls `checkOpenEXRFile(data.data(), length, ...)`. The staged PoC's OpenEXR header includes a `compression` attribute whose value byte is `0x04`, so `decompress_data()` takes `case EXR_COMPRESSION_PIZ` and `internal_exr_undo_piz()` begins reading PIZ chunk fields from attacker-controlled bytes.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan sink. `fasthuf_read_bits()` refills its bit buffer by dereferencing `*currByte` even though `currByte` has already reached `topByte`, so the byte load lands exactly one byte past the packed chunk buffer.
sink.note: Both saved AddressSanitizer reports fault at `internal_huf.c:1186` with `READ of size 1` one byte to the right of the heap region allocated for the packed chunk buffer.

root_cause.description: Root cause. After a `LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN` marker has been read, vulnerable code requests the extra 8-bit run length without first checking whether `currByte` has already reached `topByte`.
root_cause.note: The staged patch inserts `if (currByte >= topByte) ... return EXR_ERR_CORRUPT_CHUNK;` immediately before this call.

tainted_value_origin.description: The reproduced CLI path reads the PoC file from disk into `data` and forwards that byte buffer to the in-memory OpenEXR core checker.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific dispatch gate. The staged PoC's parsed `compression` attribute value is `0x04`, so chunk decompression is admitted onto the PIZ decoder path rather than ZIP/RLE/B44/DWA handling.

admitted_location.code:
rv = internal_exr_undo_piz (
    decode, packbufptr, packsz, unpackbufptr, unpacksz);

fine_trace.note: Source. After the bitmap section of the attacker-controlled PIZ chunk, the decoder reads the next 32-bit field as `hufbytes`, the byte length of the Huffman-coded payload.

This chunk-level bounds check is present and succeeds on the staged witness, so the sub-buffer `[packed + nBytes, packed + nBytes + hufbytes)` is admitted as the Huffman input for `internal_huf_decompress()`.

The Huffman decoder materializes attacker-controlled header fields from the admitted sub-buffer: the symbol range `[im, iM]` and the encoded bit count `nBits` that govern fast-table initialization and later decode length.

The decoder advances `ptr` to the Huffman table bytes after the 20-byte header, derives the declared bitstream size from `nBits`, and passes the existing size check. `fasthuf_initialize()` is then entered with `*table == ptr` and `numBytes == nCompressed - hufInfoBlockSize`.
Fast table setup computes `topByte` as the end of the admitted table buffer and enforces a present exhaustion check only before reading the initial 6-bit `codeLen` for each symbol.

On the crashing iteration the guarded 6-bit read succeeds and yields `codeLen == LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN`, selecting the branch that must consume one additional 8-bit run-length value from the same input stream.

Root-cause step. After `codeLen` identifies `LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN`, vulnerable code immediately asks for the extra 8 run-length bits but does not repeat the `currByte >= topByte` truncation check that guarded the 6-bit read.

Sink. The 8-bit request from step 7 reaches `fasthuf_read_bits()` with too few buffered bits left, so the refill loop executes and dereferences `*currByte` even though `currByte` has already reached `topByte`, producing the saved one-byte heap-buffer-overflow read.

allocation_context.note: The packed chunk buffer read by `fasthuf_read_bits()` is heap-allocated here. `sanitizer_trace.txt` reports a 99-byte region and `default_crash_trace.txt` reports a 46-byte region from a different build, but both runs fault at the same `internal_huf.c:1186` byte read.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: Stage 01 reproduction_report.json, sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, patch.diff, and the staged vulnerable worktree

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds the missing `currByte >= topByte` truncation check immediately before the reproduced `fasthuf_read_bits(8, ...)` call in the `LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN` branch, which is exactly the unchecked obligation on the crashing path.

format.name: OpenEXR file with PIZ-compressed scanline chunk and truncated fast-Huffman table data
format.contract: The witness must parse as an OpenEXR image whose `compression` attribute selects the PIZ decoder path and whose packed PIZ chunk passes the chunk-level `nBytes + hufbytes <= packsz` admission check in `internal_exr_undo_piz()`. Inside the admitted Huffman payload, `fasthuf_initialize()` must reach a symbol-table iteration where the guarded 6-bit `codeLen` read returns `LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN`, but the stream is already exhausted for the required extra 8-bit run-length read. On that exact state, vulnerable code falls from the `LONG_ZEROCODE_RUN` branch into `fasthuf_read_bits(8, ...)` without rechecking `currByte >= topByte`, and `fasthuf_read_bits()` performs the one-byte over-read reported by ASan.
